closing.consumerCatchupScope: A ready checkpoint is a readable canonical prefix, not a claim of zero chain lag. Remaining application catch-up stays with ZeeSwap.

limits: This is incident recovery, not a benchmark, uptime promise or multi-tenant capacity test.
Old catalogs pointing at reclaimed copies are no longer independent restorable snapshots. Current logical history remains intact.
Offline GC requires explicit reader coordination. No online reader-lease protocol is implemented.
Reclamation recovered space before the user approved a separate allocation change from 24 to 26 GiB. Archive headroom remains finite.
One-GiB service cgroups experienced file-cache pressure without observed OOM. Restart timings depend on concurrent work and cache state.
A ready consumer checkpoint is a readable canonical prefix, not proof that application indexing has caught up to source head.
Physical free-space measurements also include separate user-authorized cleanup outside Zeer; that space is not counted as archive reclamation.
